projects.title: Beryl
projects.summary: An installable set of repository files and scripts that tell coding agents how to work in a project and check that some of those rules were actually followed.
projects.role: Author and maintainer. I designed and wrote Beryl; this site's repository uses it.
projects.problem: Instruction files such as AGENTS.md can guide an agent, but they give no evidence that the rules were followed, and different tools read different files.
projects.method: Beryl installs one canonical instruction set with task routing and project context, plus deterministic shell checks (Markdown sanity, secret scanning, test-manifest immutability, project tests) that run locally and in optional Git hooks.
projects.decision: Checks are plain shell scripts over files in the repository rather than a hosted service or agent plugin, so any agent, CI runner, or reviewer can run the same gate and read its output.

artifact.label: Real check output from this site's repository: a test file was edited without updating the test manifest, and the Beryl gate refused it.
artifact.content:
$ printf '\n// weakened\n' >> tests/update-topic-subtitle.test.js
$ ./.beryl/scripts/check-tests-unchanged.sh
ERROR: check-tests: configured test scope differs from tests/.manifest.sha256. If intentional, run .beryl/scripts/update-test-manifest.sh and commit the updated manifest.

projects.limitation: The checks detect changes; they do not prove an agent's change is correct, and anyone with write access can update the manifest. Beryl still depends on human review and branch protection.
projects.result: Used in this repository, where the check gate runs before every change; a benchmark of whether machine-readable policies improve agent outcomes is in progress as CP3106 independent research and has no results yet.

projects.title: Notes — this site
projects.summary: The site you are reading: a static build that turns my Notion study notes into public, searchable pages while keeping math, code, and nested pages intact.
projects.role: Author and maintainer of the pipeline, templates, and notes.
projects.problem: Study notes lose value on the web when LaTeX, code indentation, nested pages, and images break, or when readers cannot tell a rough note from a checked one.
projects.method: A strict Notion ingestion step normalizes each topic tree to JSON and fails on unsupported blocks. A static build renders routes, search, RSS, and sitemap for Cloudflare, joining checked-in sidecars for publication status, corrections, and stable images.
projects.decision: Corrections and statuses live in checked-in sidecar files keyed by Notion block ids, not in the pulled JSON, so a fresh Notion pull cannot silently undo a fix.

artifact.label: One real block from the Advanced Dynamic Programming note: normalized JSON in, rendered HTML out; MathJax typesets the equation in the browser.
artifact.content:
{"type":"equation","blockId":"347d3a21-bb2d-80c2-ab57-e88305c8b7ac", "expression":"opt[i][j-1] ≤ opt[i][j] ≤ opt[i+1][j]"}
\[opt[i][j-1] ≤ opt[i][j] ≤ opt[i+1][j]\]

projects.limitation: Most notes are unreviewed Working notes. Four images had to be redrawn because the Notion originals were no longer reachable. Page speed was measured only locally with a throttled phone profile (Home: about 0.6 s to largest paint, 47 KB transferred) and is not monitored in production.
projects.result: 125 note pages and 19 posts build from checked-in data with deterministic tests; every note shows its publication status and substantive corrections are published on the Errata page.

projects.title: SIAP
projects.summary: Structure and Interpretation of Agentic Patterns: a book in progress that teaches agent systems by building interpreters for reasoning and tool-use loops.
projects.role: Author. I write the manuscript and maintain its build scripts.
projects.problem: Agent engineering is often held together by framework defaults and prompt folklore, leaving objectives, memory, tool contracts, and failure modes under-specified.
projects.method: Markdown chapters connect decision theory, planning, retrieval, safety, and multi-agent coordination to small interpreters. Python scripts build a static web reader and PDF, and audit citations and visuals.
projects.decision: Teach by construction: each pattern is introduced as a small interpreter the reader can run and break, rather than as a framework recipe.

artifact.label: Manuscript state from the repository on 2026-09-30.
items: 4 parts: Foundations of Agency, Reasoning Architectures, Tool Use and Embodiment, Multi-Agent Systems
36 chapter files, about 57,000 words of draft text
Web reader and PDF built by the repository's scripts

projects.limitation: This is an unfinished draft with no external review or publisher; chapters vary in completeness and the interpreters have not been evaluated with readers.
projects.result: The draft is readable online and the build checks citation and visual rules on every change.

projects.title: AI Society Corpus
projects.summary: An interactive knowledge graph for NUS AI Society that links AI/ML study topics by prerequisites, shared tags, and backlinks.
projects.role: Initial author and main contributor: I wrote the first build and 30 of the 82 commits in the repository as of August 2026; other society members contribute topics and fixes.
projects.problem: AI/ML learners need to see how concepts depend on and relate to one another, not just read a long list of topics.
projects.method: Topics live in validated Markdown with structured frontmatter. A static Astro build derives prerequisite, tag-similarity (Jaccard), and WikiLink-backlink edges and renders them with React and a D3 force graph.
projects.decision: Relationships are computed at build time from the Markdown rather than curated by hand, so a new topic joins the graph through its frontmatter alone.

artifact.label: The live graph and its source.
items: Content validation, unit tests, and Playwright checks run in the repository
6 topic files published at the time of writing

projects.limitation: The corpus is small so far, and tag-similarity edges are inferred: two topics that share tags are linked even when the relationship is weak.
projects.result: Readers can move through a navigable concept network, and contributors get a reviewable workflow with validation.
